description: Online shop checkout. 15 sections; REQ-CO-06 is a compound to split, giving 16 expected requirements. Ambiguous: REQ-CO-07, CO-11, CO-15.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow a user to add a product to their cart from the product page.
The system shall only allow a cart item's quantity to be a whole number from 1 to 10.
The system shall allow a user to remove an item from their cart.
The system shall keep a logged-in user's cart contents across sessions, including after logging out and back in.
The system shall allow a user to complete checkout as a guest without creating an account.
The system shall validate the shipping address against the postal service's address database.
requirements.note: First half of a compound: REQ-CO-06 joins validating and saving with "and", two independent capabilities, and should be split.

requirements.statement: The system shall save a validated shipping address to the user's address book.
requirements.note: Second half of the REQ-CO-06 compound.

requirements.statement: The checkout should not take too many steps.
requirements.ambiguityReason: "Too many steps" sets no maximum, so there's no pass/fail threshold.
requirements.note: No obviously vague adjective, so it's the hardest ambiguity to detect; a keyword-based checker misses it.

requirements.statement: Before payment, the system shall show an order summary with each item, the subtotal, the delivery fee, and the total.
The system shall process credit and debit card payments through a PCI-compliant third-party payment processor.
If a payment is declined, the system shall show the decline reason returned by the payment processor.

requirements.ambiguityReason: "Fast" has no time limit, so it can't be measured.

requirements.statement: The system shall charge no delivery fee for orders with a subtotal of €50.00 or more, and a flat €4.95 fee below that.
requirements.note: One pricing rule with a threshold and its two outcomes: should NOT be split.

requirements.statement: The system shall display an estimated delivery date based on the shipping method the user selects.
The system shall send an order confirmation email with an itemized receipt within 5 minutes of a successful payment.
The checkout experience should be smooth and intuitive.
requirements.ambiguityReason: "Smooth and intuitive" is subjective; there's no usability measure (task time, error rate, success rate) to test.

boundaries.why: The allowed range: 1 and 10 accepted, 0 and 11 rejected. Only the upper edge (10 or 11) or 0 counts as evidence, because a quantity of 1 appears in almost every ordinary cart test.
examples: When the user sets the quantity to 11
When the user enters 0 as the quantity
counterExamples: When the user sets the quantity to 3

boundaries.why: Exactly €50.00 must be free; €49.99 must pay the €4.95 fee.
